newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov Pataki sees Niagara Falls gaining 750 jobs.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov Pataki sees Niagara Falls gaining 750 jobs.

text.p: New York State Gov. George Pataki on Wednesday, heralding his Administration's success in attracting business, said TeleTech Holdings signed a lease for a $10 million phone center in Niagara Falls.

The company plans to hire 750 new workers for the 65,000 square-foot center at Falls Street Faire. The center will offer businesses various telecommunications services, from making airline reservations to using technology to assist with customer service.
"This is the largest influx of new jobs to Niagara Falls in nearly a century and it is no coincidence," said Pataki in prepared remarks, pointing to the state's economic rebound.
A spokesman for the governor said that company officials anticipated opening the center fairly rapidly.

TeleTech will get $700,000 in loans and grants from the state's Jobs Now Fund, a $400,000 interest subsidy grant and a $300,000 skills training grant from Empire State Development, which helped persuade the company to expand in New York.
Further, the company will get a $1 million loan from the New York Power Authority's Niagara Economic Development Fund.
